claims.notes: The comment says TestFailureIfGitBackupDirUndefined would still pass if the GIT_BACKUP_DIR guard were removed, because it accepts any error from Run. True: the test asserts only require.Errorf(t, Run(), ...). Without the guard, validateStartupConfig would go on to os.Stat(""), which returns a not-exist error, so Run would still fail. The fault is the loose assertion at backup_test.go:819. The PR's description and commit message say backup_test.go changes only removed TestPublicGitLabRepositoryBackup2 and simplified TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup, so this assertion was not edited. The change moved the guard into validateStartupConfig with the same check in the same order ('Behaviour ... unchanged'), so the test was just as loose before and after. The guard itself does the right thing, so the fault is not on a line the change rewrote. This is outside the change. It does not concern LFS or _FILE handling, so PE-q1 does not apply. It is not referred as a pre-existing candidate: the user-facing guard and its message still work, and a test that never pinned the message breaks no outcome the project promised to users.
